hints.text: Two facts to memorize: $\frac{d}{dx}\sin x = \cos x$ and $\frac{d}{dx}\cos x = -\sin x$. Watch the minus sign on the second one.
$g'(x) = 2\cos x - \sin x$. Now substitute $x = 0$, using $\cos 0 = 1$ and $\sin 0 = 0$.

explanation: Differentiate term by term: $\frac{d}{dx}(2\sin x) = 2\cos x$ and $\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it off the graphs
steps: Near $x = 0$, $\sin x$ looks like the line $y = x$ (slope $1$), so $2\sin x$ has slope $2$ there.
Near $x = 0$, $\cos x$ is at the top of its hill: flat, slope $0$.
Add the slopes: $2 + 0 = 2$. Same answer, no formula needed.
